article_title: A systematic review of the key components of online peer feedback practices in higher education
citation: Xingshi Gao, Omid Noroozi, Judith Gulikers, Harm J.A. Biemans, Seyyed Kazem Banihashem. (2024). A systematic review of the key components of online peer feedback practices in higher education. Educational Research Review. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.edurev.2023.100588
title: Corpus of 73 peer-reviewed studies on online peer feedback in higher education (2000–2022)
description: The review's evidence base is a corpus of 73 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2000 and 2022, identified through searches of Scopus, ERIC, and Web of Science following PRISMA guidelines. The review reports that "The number of participants involved in the reviewed publications varied from 3 to 2421" and that more than half of the studies (n = 39) were conducted in Asian areas, particularly Taiwan (n = 21; 28%). Content analysis (n = 34; 47%) and questionnaires (n = 31; 42%) were the most regularly used data collection instruments.
requirements: Included articles focused on feedback between students, were performed in online or blended environments, included empirical experiments, and were conducted in higher education
constraints: Only peer-reviewed journal articles in English were included; studies not investigating written feedback comments were excluded
target_learning_goals: peer feedback practices in online settings
examples: Inter-rater reliability was checked with Kappa results (κ = 0.86, p < .001) at the title/abstract stage and (κ = 0.68, p < .001) at full-text screening
